newsitem.title: JAPAN: Artificial bid to halt yen's fall could fail--Muto.
newsitem.headline: Artificial bid to halt yen's fall could fail--Muto.

text.p: Japanese cabinet minister Kabun Muto said on Friday that any "artificial" attempt to check a further fall in the yen could fail in the current environment of a continuing capital outflow from Japan.

"An artificial attempt to check a further slide by the yen may not yield any result, given that Japan's low interest rates are pushing Japanese capital abroad," said Muto, who is director-general of Management and Coordination Agency.

"Considering the massive amount of money circulating around the world, intervention by the BOJ would not be enough to affect global fund flows. Japan should change the current interest rate structure," Muto told reporters.
Japan should increase its official discount rate (ODR) by the end of this year to discourage capital outflows from Japan, he said.
Muto said that there was nothing wrong with the dollar moving above 125 yen, adding that in terms of purchasing-power parity, 150 yen to the dollar would be appropriate.
